### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class), SysMetadataRepository (symbol, a top-level class), NOT_OVERRIDABLE (literal, a string literal in assertAllowed), /actions/_activation/:object/:action (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /api/v1/actions/_activation/:object/:action (route, a path literal in action), /api/v1/automation/:name/clone (route, a path literal in flow), /api/v1/automation/:name/toggle (route, a path literal in flow), /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set (route, a path literal in permission), /automation/:name/clone (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line), /automation/:name/toggle (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/data/sys_permission_set (route, a path literal in permission))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via automation.toggle (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /automation/:name/toggle), /api/v1/automation/:name/toggle (route, a path literal in flow), /automation/:name/toggle (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `919f1deef732b25a0eb70f6e8f2e44510f2dfd93` — the merge of head `9c169378a40971eb723e266d26be0482fef5fb27` into base `2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 919f1deef732b25a0eb70f6e8f2e44510f2dfd93 && git checkout 919f1deef732b25a0eb70f6e8f2e44510f2dfd93
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4 9c169378a40971eb723e266d26be0482fef5fb27 && git checkout -B drift-repro 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4 && git merge --no-ff 9c169378a40971eb723e266d26be0482fef5fb27

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2f2fa11d756f665a4c06160480c1dce15b9d67a4` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `9c169378a40971eb723e266d26be0482fef5fb27`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #20910 (body and all 7 comments: the pointer 5916662651, triage 5916763169, the unlock 5922075346, the claim 5922498707, the round-0 report 5923498345, the seat answer 5923536089 and the round-1 report 5924033416); PR #21026 (body, its 9-file list, and the net diff against the merge base with `origin/main`, 2f2fa11d7: 839 insertions, 114 deletions); the 42 check-runs on the head. Read-only shape held: the diff was taken with git fetch and git diff on the shared checkout, sources were read with git show and git grep, and nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

The accept-set — which writes are refused, with which code and status — is unchanged at all three doors; only the prose of a refusal moves. Each judgment named:

1. Package door (`protocol.ts` `refusePackagedBaseOverride` / `refusePackagedBaseRemoval`, environment-scoped kernel): the only change is the class-private `packagedBaseRegimeSentence` becoming the module function of the same name, with the same `?? legacy sentence` fallback for a type without a row. Predicate, `NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, 403 untouched. RIGHT.
2. Type door (`SysMetadataRepository.assertAllowed`): the new branch sits after the registry limbs, after the named-base limb and after `if (hatchOpen) return;`, guarded by `intent !== 'runtime-only'`, and throws the same `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403 that the legacy throw below it threw for the same predicate; `runtime-only` keeps `NOT_CREATABLE` and the legacy prose. `assertDeleteAllowed` still returns early for `OVERLAY_CAPABLE_TYPES` (the permission carve-out) before reaching it. The sentence's claim "provided by a code package" is sound: every protocol caller derives the intent as `artifactBacked ? 'override-artifact' : 'runtime-only'` (six sites in `protocol.ts`), so the branch is reached only for an artifact-backed name. RIGHT.
3. Named-base `ITEM_LOCKED` limb (`readOnlyBaseOverrideError`): the row prescription is consulted only when `hatchOpen` is false and the type has a row; otherwise the message is the pre-existing text byte for byte. `code`, `status`, `lockSource`, `packageId` and `docs` lie outside the hunk and are unchanged; the signature `(type, packageId, hatchOpen = false)` is unchanged. RIGHT.
4. Table shape (`packaged-base-regime.ts`): rows `{ regime, routes }`, the union type refuses a row naming neither route, the builder composes from the row alone (no type branch in any door's prose), `flow` byte-identical and pinned literally, `action` the switch only, `permission` the clone only. One regime, per-type routes, as triage directed. RIGHT.
5. Routes named exist and are spelled as served: `POST /actions/_activation/:object/:action` with object-less actions under `'global'` (`packages/runtime/src/domains/actions.ts`); the `/automation/:name/clone` and `/toggle` routes unchanged from #20819; the permission row is character-for-character the update-branch parenthetical of `PackagedPermissionSetLockedError` in `plugin-security`, itself `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` / 403. No route is added or changed anywhere in the diff. RIGHT.
6. Public surface: the new module is not re-exported from `src/index.ts`; `package.json` `exports` is `"."` only and `files` is `dist` only, so its exported symbols are internal. `assertAllowed` and `assertDeleteAllowed` were `private` at the merge base and remain `private`; their new parameters are not a public-surface change. The three removed `private static` members on `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation` are not consumer-callable. RIGHT.
7. Controls: `object` and `page` at the package door (the new `object` removal control included), `object` at the type door, `page` at the named-base limb (the moved #8146 pin) keep their sentences byte for byte; the #7426 delete-rewrap pin now partitions by `packagedBaseRegimeRow`, every other type's assertion unchanged. RIGHT.
8. Docs (`content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`): the new prose states what the head does — the three rows, the operator-only clause, `:object` = `global`, "`403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE` for a write that names no base, `403 ITEM_LOCKED` for one that names the read-only package", and "which writes are refused, and with which code, is unchanged". The narrowed first paragraph (a create aimed at a read-only package is asked to pick or create a writable base) matches `readOnlyBaseCreateError`'s "not a writable base" text. The anchor slug matches the new heading (Check Documentation Links green). Two precision notes, neither a false statement: (a) "locked against removal" for a flow or an action is a 403 at the environment-scoped door and at the repository door; on a host-config kernel a DELETE with no overlay row is the pre-existing 200 "already at artifact default" no-op (the dev measured it on the booted showcase), so the base is unremovable either way but not always refused; (b) where `plugin-security` is loaded its authoring gate answers a permission-set write first, with `NOT_OVERRIDABLE` for both the package-less and `?package=` shapes, naming the same clone — the page describes the metadata-protocol doors, and that precedence predates the PR. RIGHT, with those notes.
9. Checks on the head: 42 check-runs, all completed; 36 success, 6 skipped (Auto Label and Check PR Size on the second trigger, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke opt-in), 0 failed, 0 in_progress. Test Core (6 shards), Build Core, every Type Check lane, Lint and Repo Gates, Dogfood (3 shards), Temporal Conformance, Build Docs, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, and the four governance checks on both triggers are success. Nothing waited on.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20910-regime-c-action-permission-paths.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': patch`. RIGHT — the only released package whose source changes is `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`; `packages/rest` gains a test file only, so nothing publishes from it; `content/docs` is not a package. A refusal-text fix in a released package takes `patch`, never `skip-changeset`. The changeset body describes the three doors and the unchanged codes, and needs no migration.

Clause-②: no — RIGHT. The PR body's second line is `Clause-②: no`, the changeset carries the same line, and the diff moves no exported signature and adds no public symbol (judgment 6): no accept-set change, so no `yes`, and neither arm. The seat answer's stop (a) did not fire.

### ③ Boundary flags

Round-0 `open_questions` (report 5923498345), both ruled by seat answer 5923536089 and both implemented within its stated boundaries:

- Q1 → A. The named-base limb speaks for the row with the hatch CLOSED only. Checked on the diff: the hatch-OPEN remedy is the pre-existing text verbatim (pinned: named base, hatch OPEN); `code`, `status`, `lockSource`, `packageId`, `docs` untouched (pinned with `docs: 'docs/adr/0010-metadata-protection-model.md'`); NARROW untouched — a package-less hatch write of a Regime C type still lands `package_id: null` (pinned); the #8146 hatch-closed pin moved to `page`, a type with no row, measured to the same limb, with a Regime C pin beside it whose comment cites ADR-0126 §2. The answer said "such as object or job"; `page` meets the stated condition (regime-less, same limb). ANSWERED.
- Q2 → A. The type door answers the row sentence for `override-artifact` with the hatch closed; every type without a row keeps the list-and-hatch sentence (pinned on `object`). Stop (a), an exported signature moving, did not fire (judgment 6). Stop (b), a no-row type changing its sentence at any door, did not fire (judgment 7). ANSWERED.

Round-1 report (5924033416): `open_questions` empty. Its deviations:

- Two test files beyond the amended surface, both test-only in `packages/metadata-protocol`: one required by the ruling (the moved pin and its neighbour), one by the partition. ACCEPTED.
- A docs subsection added beyond the two corrected sentences: judged in ① item 8. ACCEPTED, with the two precision notes.
- A tool-stamped refresh line in the PR body; the worktree rebuilt with no diff. Cosmetic, no diff. ACCEPTED.

Acceptance note and out-of-scope finding (both rounds): the permission row copies `plugin-security`'s parenthetical and nothing pins the two spellings equal across packages. Verified equal on this head (judgment 5). A drift pin needs a home that imports both packages, which `metadata-protocol` cannot be. ESCALATED as a non-blocking follow-up for the seat to file or decline; it does not gate this head.

Docs-drift-check (PR comment 5923480340): one hand-written page named and corrected here; four release-owned pages named, none in the file list. HELD.

Dispatch fences (claim 5922498707): the hatch's fate and the other regimes' sentences (#15206) untouched — no sentence outside the three Regime C rows changes at any door; no route added or changed. HELD.
